nodes.description: Sural nerve biopsy shows a selective absence of large myelinated fibers with a normal density/complement of small myelinated fibers and, in most cases, no primary axonal degeneration; overt demyelinating change is variable and has been seen only in some (younger) patients. This selective large-fiber deficit is the diagnostic pathological hallmark of the entity.

nodes.description: The primary lesion is a lack of large-caliber neurons in the dorsal root ganglia (large sensory neurons) and the spinal anterior horns (large motor neurons), demonstrated at autopsy. A developmental abnormality with faulty neuronal growth, followed by axonal atrophy, is the proposed (still hypothetical) basis for the selective loss of the large-fiber population.

evidence.reference_title: Hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy with absence of large myelinated fibers due to absence of large neurons in dorsal root ganglia and anterior horns, clinically associated with deafness, mental retardation, and epilepsy (HMSN-ADM).
evidence.snippet: The autopsy showed complete absence of large myelinated fibers in peripheral motor and sensory nerves corresponding to a lack of large neurons in dorsal root ganglia and anterior horns of the spinal cord, moderate neurogenic muscle atrophy, and nearly complete absence of neurons in the dentate nucleus of the cerebellum.

evidence.snippet: We infer from our findings that a developmental abnormality with faulty growth and subsequent axonal atrophy may be responsible.

nodes.description: An early-onset, slowly progressive hereditary motor and sensory (poly)neuropathy is the defining clinical feature, with marked slowing of motor and sensory conduction and absent sensory action potentials on electrophysiology.

evidence.snippet: We describe two brothers, 11 and 13 years old, respectively, with an early-onset hereditary motor and sensory neuropathy, deafness, and mental retardation.
